fronts.question: Determine whether uniform FO(TC) policy descriptions admit a polynomially checkable proof of worst-case comparison depth at the antichain root, rather than just polynomial evaluation on a single input order.
fronts.falsifier: Construct an explicit FO(TC)-expressible policy whose worst-case comparison budget is hard to check or whose all-n expressive completeness provably fails.
fronts.implication: A sound, complete and polynomial-size proof-carrying FO(TC) normal form would establish SORT-BOUND-U membership in NP; execution alone does not.
fronts.basis: Founder-selected Antonina issue JTsW4AnxTLzN18IBQibXea-fervor and SoringP1 issue #301; previous certificate soundness-versus-completeness gap.

fronts.question: Test a candidate exact root-reachable equivalence of optimal comparison histories stronger than relabelled-poset isomorphism, with an explicitly checkable two-outcome congruence and a polynomial bound on distinct classes for all n.
fronts.falsifier: Exhibit an infinite family of root-optimal decision strategies for which any such equivalence requires superpolynomially many distinct verified classes, or prove a concrete simpler class fails.
fronts.implication: A correct polynomial root-optimal quotient plus a locally checkable height certificate would yield a polynomial NP certificate for the unary decision threshold.
fronts.basis: Framed DAG checker in scripts/check_framed_strategy.py; prior work distinguishes a valid local checker from an all-n completeness theorem.

fronts.question: Seek a compositional exact recurrence for optimal sorting from chain or ordinal-product interfaces that preserves the adversarial root and both sibling branches, not merely the post-transcript minimax F(P).
fronts.falsifier: Supply a small but extensible family in which all candidate interface summaries agree but the exact antichain root optimum differs, or show an explicit sibling-incompatibility obstruction.
fronts.implication: A uniform polynomial-state exact root recurrence would improve the time bound for computing S(n) and perhaps place SORT-BOUND-U in P.
fronts.basis: docs/problem.md, established root-prefix sibling obstruction and prior failed naive direct-sum transfer in the research ledger.

fronts.question: Construct and rigorously analyze a uniform exact evaluation algorithm for S(n) with asymptotically smaller workspace than the existing recurrence, explicitly accounting for representation and branch recomputation.
fronts.falsifier: Give a concrete state family forcing the proposed compact representation to store superpolynomial independent decisions, or find a hidden recursive stack-space violation.
fronts.implication: A verified uniform smaller-space bound would strengthen the known upper bound for SORT-BOUND-U even without proving P or NP membership.
fronts.basis: docs/problem.md established unary PSPACE membership and prior recomputation analyses; focus on a genuinely improved bound.

fronts.question: Construct a sound, polynomial-time checkable adversary invariant that forces a comparison obstruction from the initial n-element antichain under EVERY sorting strategy, not only from an arbitrary reachable partial order.
fronts.falsifier: Construct a uniform sorter counterstrategy defeating a proposed local forcing invariant even though isolated reachable gadget states remain hard.
fronts.implication: A verified all-n antichain lower-bound theorem can improve numerical bounds on S(n), but would not alone separate unary computation complexity classes.
fronts.basis: Root quantifier distinction in GitHub issues #47 and #48 and previously established small-poset lower-bound gadgets.
